messages.subject: The R Statistical JSON server
messages.body_plain:
So to stimulate some discussion, is anyone interested in doing this?
The idea is really simple:

1: Provide a Rook applications that executes a given R function and
returns the result in JSON format.

2. The url will look something like http://example.com/srv/rnorm or
http://example.com/srv/base::rnorm.

3. Input can be CGI GET or POST variables when sensible. For instance
http://example.com/srv/rnorm?n=1&mean=100&sd=.5

4. Input can be as a JSON object via POST payload.

5. Output is a JSON object.

I've spoken with various individuals who are or have worked on
something like this, and I think it really needs to be standardized.
Also, which package is better for implementing this: RJSONIO or rjson.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: The R Statistical JSON server
messages.body_plain:
Well, I always do that "by hand"... i.e. when I was building a RApache
app, I used to save results as a list, then serialized them with
toJSON. Of course, you can serialize pretty much anything with JSON.
About form serialization, I use jQuery's .serialize() method. You just
need appropriate form selector, and you're good to go: $
("form").serialize()
The function returns a string in "n=1&mean=100&sd=.5" format (like in
GET request).

I'm not sure if I could carry out such a project from scratch, but if
you're looking for a guinea pig/collaborator/alpha|beta-tester/etc.
I'm in! =) Anyway, did you provide "rnorm" deliberately, or as a
meaningful "foobar" replacement? I hope that you have something
specific in mind (and I should definitely port my RApache app to Rook,
I'm being lazy as hell!!!)

Oh, and, I vote for RJSONIO, since it's faster. At least they say so
on package page:

This is an alternative to rjson package. That version is too slow for
converting large R objects to JSON and is not extensible, but a very
useful prototype. It is fast for parsing. This package uses methods,
vectorized operations and C code and callbacks to R functions for
deserializing JSON objects to R. Verison 0.4 of this package uses a
new native parser, implements the transformation code in C and
allocates memory efficiently (rather than concatenating because of
event driven parsing). The result is a significantly faster parsing of
large JSON documents.

messages.subject: Re: The R Statistical JSON server
messages.body_plain:
OK, so it's not that problematic to incorporate JSON parser in Rook, but as Jeroen said, one should stick to (R)Apache because it's reliable. I can compare node.js with Rook - they're both great tools and have great potential, since you're using one standard (language) only to handle HTTP requests, but c'mon, Apache exists (and is being used by millions) for a good reason!

Jeroen, I guess you're using several R scripts and GET superglobal in RApache to generate stuff. And something tells me that you're running this on your local machine (it took 2s to generate ggplot graph). =)

Anyway, about Rook JSON server... I'm afraid that I don't have much leisure time to spend on writing this one from scratch, but if you need an errand boy, just lemme know!

messages.subject: Announcing gWidgetsWWW2
messages.body_plain:
As some of you know, gWidgets is a relatively simple interface between
the R programmer and several different graphical toolkits (RGtk2,
tcltk, Qt). Its goal is to make it easy to write simple to somewhat
complex GUIs for R without having to know the details of GUI
programming (in this case, the details of HTML/JavaScript/JSON/
CSS/...).

This is to announce the *new* package gWidgetsWWW2 which is built
using Rook. This is a rewrite of the older gWidgetsWWW package
currently on CRAN. This new package is available for now from r-forge:

https://r-forge.r-project.org/R/?group_id=761

or for the impatient, this command might work:

install.packages("gWidgetsWWW2", repos="http://R-Forge.R-
project.org <http://project.org>")

With this package, writing interactive web interfaces for local use is
as easy as writing this script:

w <- gwindow("simple web app")
b <- gbutton("click me", cont=w)
addHandlerClicked(b, handler=function(h,...) {
  galert("Ouch, that hurt", parent=w)
})

This script would be called with

load_app("scriptname.R")

The package has a demo (demo("gWidgetsWWW2")) that shows many simple
examples. Feedback is most welcome. The package has little testing so
far. (Only on the browsers available with my Mac -- so perhaps it
works with IE, but I'm not sure.) The package uses the ExtJS
JavaScript libraries from www.sencha.com <http://www.sencha.com> (although 3.3.0, not the
newest 4.0). These come with the package.

As with gWidgetsWWW, when Rook integrates with rapache, this too will
work with rapache to serve pages to the public. For now, it is limited
to local use.

--John

Just for fun, here is how one way to do this with gWidgetsWWW2:

f <- tempfile()
width <- height <- 400

make_plot <- function(a, lb, ub) {
  if(is.na <http://is.na>(a) || is.na <http://is.na>(lb) || is.na <http://is.na>(ub))
    return()

  canvas(f, width=width, height=height)
  FUN <- function(x) x^a
  curve(FUN, lb, ub)
  dev.off()
  svalue(cv) <- f                       # assign to gcanvas object
}

w <- gwindow("Plot example")
gstatusbar("Powered by gWidgetsWWW2 and Rook", cont=w)
pg <- gpanedgroup(cont=w)
cv <- gcanvas(width=width, height=height, cont=pg)

g <- gframe("Parameters:", cont=pg, horizontal=FALSE)
tbl <- glayout(cont=g)
tbl[1,1] <- "a:"
tbl[1,2] <- (a <- gedit("1", cont=tbl))
tbl[2,1] <- "lower:"
tbl[2,2] <- (lb <- gedit("0", cont=tbl))
tbl[3,1] <- "upper:"
tbl[3,2] <- (ub <- gedit("2", cont=tbl))
visible(tbl) <- TRUE

gseparator(cont=g)
b <- gbutton("plot", cont=g)

plotHandler <- function(h,...) {
  vals <- sapply(list(a, lb, ub), function(i) as.numeric(svalue(i)),
simplify=FALSE)
  do.call("make_plot", vals)
}
addHandlerClicked(b, handler=plotHandler)
## initial plot
plotHandler(NULL)

messages.subject: Re: The R Statistical JSON server
messages.body_plain:
This is on github as well, but posting here to discuss:

# https://github.com/jeffreyhorner/rRack/blob/master/Rook/inst/exampleApps/RJSONIO.R

library(RJSONIO)
app <- function(env){
    req <- Request$new(env)
    res <- Response$new()

    obj <- sub('^/','',req$path_info())

    # Get out of here fast if no object exists
    if (!exists(obj)) return(res$finish())

#    res$write(paste(capture.output(str(req
$params()),file=NULL),collapse='\n'))
#    return(res$finish())

    # Gather args from one of three sources: GET, POST as a x-www-
urlencoded,
    # or POST as JSON payload. params() squishes GET and POST together
when
    # POST is x-www-urlencoded.
    if (!is.null(req$params())) {
	args <- req$params()
    } else {
	# TODO: Collect POST payload and pass to RJSONIO
	args <- list()
    }

    # Normalize arguments to R types if necessary. Integers to
integer, Numerics to numeric, etc.
    # Maybe we can propose a vector syntax in CGI that's coherent,
too.
    for (i in names(args)){

	# Keep as character anything that starts with a quote char
	if (grepl('^[\'"]',args[[i]]))
	    next

	# Integer
	if (grepl('^[+-]?\\d+$',args[[i]]))
	    args[[i]] <- as.integer(args[[i]])

	# Numeric. need to add scientific notation
	if (grepl('^[+-]?[0-9.]+$',args[[i]]))
	    args[[i]] <- as.numeric(args[[i]])
    }

    if (is.function(get(obj)))
	res$write(toJSON(do.call(obj,args)))
    else
	res$write(toJSON(get(obj)))

    res$finish()

}
